content:
Apple continues its efforts to fight back against the UK government's mandated encryption backdoor, according to a new report by the Financial Times.

Tim Bradshaw reports that Apple has launched a new legal challenge against the UK government's attempt to force access to users' encrypted data, filed in July.

The report details how Apple has recently been pushing back against the UK government's efforts to weaken encryption protections for Apple users in the country.

The dispute began in early 2025, when the UK government secretly ordered Apple to provide access to data protected by Advanced Data Protection for iCloud users worldwide.

Because Apple does not hold the encryption keys, complying with the order would require weakening or redesigning the service.

Apple's response was to stop allowing new UK users to enable Advanced Data Protection and to challenge the order at the Investigatory Powers Tribunal.

The company stressed that it has never built and will never build any backdoor or master key.

Under US pressure, the UK ultimately withdrew its demand regarding US users. However, it was later revealed that the original global order had been replaced by one targeting only UK users.

For more details, read the Financial Times' full report today.
